title: Adaptive Sample Synthesis and Telemetry Protocol
author: Amina Patel
content:
Overview
========

This document describes the Adaptive Sample Synthesis and Telemetry Protocol (ASSTP), a standardized process for synthesizing, selecting, and instrumenting prompt/response samples used across evaluation, onboarding, and regression triage activities. The protocol unifies practices used by the eval harness, prompt catalog, model onboarding team, quantization profiling, and the regression triage playbooks to ensure samples are: representative, debuggable, and traceable to production telemetry.

Purpose and scope
------------------
- Purpose: create a repeatable, telemetry-driven mechanism to select and synthesize evaluation samples that (1) maximize coverage of real-world workload behaviors, (2) prioritize failure modes relevant to production, and (3) embed metadata required for fast triage and root cause analysis.
- Scope: this protocol applies to offline evals, continuous benchmark scans, pre-promotion onboarding suites, and regression triage (shadow and field evals). It covers sample synthesis, telemetry signal mapping, labeling contract, bench configuration, and integration points with model release pipelines.

Key principles
--------------
1. Telemetry-first selection: real production request fingerprints drive sample prioritization.
2. Stratified diversity: maintain controlled strata (e.g., short/medium/long context, language, user-intent class, prior-token-distribution) to avoid blind spots.
3. Fail-first amplification: when telemetry shows recurring error categories (timeouts, hallucinations, truncation artifacts), amplify similar synthetic probes to increase statistical power.
4. Traceability: each sample must carry provenance metadata linking back to telemetry IDs, model version, and routing policy.
5. Minimal syntactic perturbation: synthetic variants should minimally alter semantics to measure stability vs brittleness.

Telemetry signals and mapping
---------------------------
Collect the following signals from production for use in sample generation and prioritization:
- request_id (unique per-request)
- route_id and model_variant (routing metadata)
- token_count_in and effective_context_window
- latency_ms (p50/p95/p99 distribution slice)
- error_class (e.g., user_reject, generation_abort, api_timeout, policy_reject)
- response_entropy_est (server-side estimate)
- kv_cache_hit_rate or prefix_reuse_score
- user_locale and top_intent_cluster (from intent tagging pipeline)

Map telemetry to strata rules:
- short_context: token_count_in < 64
- medium_context: 64 <= token_count_in < 512
- long_context: token_count_in >= 512
- high_latency_hotspot: latency_ms > route_p99_threshold AND traffic_weight > 0.1%
- high_error_density: error_class != null AND error_rate_in_last_24h > 0.5%

Sample synthesis algorithm (high level)
-------------------------------------
1. Fingerprint sampling: daily pull of N=2000 candidate requests weighted by recency and by a telemetry anomaly score (anomaly = normalized(latency) + normalized(error_indicator) + novelty_score).
2. Stratum assignment: assign each candidate to a stratum using mapping rules.
3. Fail amplification: for strata with error density above amplification_threshold (default 0.3%), create syntactic variants for each request producing M variations:
   - minimal paraphrase (preserve intent, reword)
   - tokenization boundary shift (insert filler tokens or punctuation to alter tokenization alignment)
   - prefix-sentence-reordering (for multi-sentence prompts)
   - context-append noise (append unrelated short sentence)
4. Stability variants: for a random subset (20%) generate randomized decode seed variations to test stochastic stability.
5. Label assignment: attach labeling tasks for a human or assisted annotator depending on error_class presence.
6. Output package: produce a bench shard with metadata (see Bench config table).

Labeling contract and quality rules
----------------------------------
- If telemetry indicates error_class is present, sample enters a high-priority labeling queue with "triage_metadata" fields prefilled.
- Label schema (CSV/JSONL fields): sample_id, provenance_ids (list), prompt_text, expected_behavior (free text), failure_tag (enum), severity (low/med/high), annotator_notes.
- Minimum label coverage per shard: 1k samples or 10% labeled, whichever is first.
- Inter-annotator agreement target: Cohen's kappa >= 0.7 for binary failure tags.

Bench config and requirements (table as plain text)
--------------------------------------------------
Name | Purpose | Default params | Owner
-----|---------|----------------|------
asstp_shard_v1 | runtime bench shard for continuous scan | batch_size=32, seeds_per_sample=3, time_budget_hours=6 | eval-harness
asstp_onboard_qa | pre-promotion high-fidelity check | batch_size=8, deterministic=True, label_quota=500 | model-onboarding
asstp_regression_probe | triage-focused probe set | targeted_strata=high_error_density, amplification_factor=5 | regression-team

Integration with model onboarding and quant profiles
----------------------------------------------------
- Pre-promotion: require model to pass asstp_onboard_qa with no new high-severity failures on core slices and <=2% aggregate regression vs baseline on stability index.
- Quantization: when running quant profiling, include asstp_regression_probe with long_context and tokenization-shift variants to detect quant-induced decoding artifacts.
- Shadow testing: produce a daily shadow shard mapped to live traffic routes for production continuity checks.

Metrics and SLOs for the protocol
--------------------------------
- Coverage SLO: at least 95% of active routes have an ASSTP shard within the last 72 hours.
- Amplification recall: 90% recall for top-3 recurring production failure signatures in subsequent amplification run.
- Labeling lag: 80% of high-priority labeled samples annotated within 48 hours.
- Stability index: per-sample entropy variance <= baseline_threshold (set per-model family during onboarding).

Operational procedures and step-by-step workflows
------------------------------------------------
1. Daily ingestion job (owned by eval-harness):
   - Pull telemetry blob from telemetry-store for the last 48 hours.
   - Run fingerprint sampler with weighting config file (see CLI example).
   - Emit candidate list and create shard artifact in bench-bucket.
2. Labeling cascade (owned by applied-ml-ops):
   - High-priority queue -> human annotators (triage team)
   - Medium -> assisted labeling (LLM pre-label, human verify)
   - Low -> crowdsourced verification / automated heuristics.
3. Pre-promotion gate (owned by model-onboarding):
   - Run asstp_onboard_qa; attach results to promotion ticket.
   - If failure_severity >= high, block promotion and trigger regression-bisect automation.
4. Regression triage fast-path (owned by regression-team):
   - If new failure cluster detected in production, run targeted amplification with amplification_factor=10 on the last 7 days.
   - Use sample provenance to correlate with deployment events, quant profiles, or routing changes.

Rollout checklist for teams
--------------------------
- [ ] Telemetry schema implemented and exported to telemetry-store (fields above).
- [ ] Eval-harness daily job deployed and monitoring alerts configured (failure rate of job > 5%).
- [ ] Labeling queues and annotator contracts updated to accept triage_metadata.
- [ ] Onboarding gate updated to require ASSTP pass.
- [ ] Documentation link added to release playbook for on-call engineers.

Traceability and artifact naming conventions
-----------------------------------------
- shard artifact name: asstp.{date}.{routeid}.{model_family}.{stratum}.{shardseq}
- sample_id: asstp-s.{YYYYMMDD}.{shorthash}
- provenance_ids: list of production request_ids (comma separated) with primary_prov flagged.

CLI and example snippets
------------------------
Fingerprint sampling CLI (example):
    redwood-eval fingerprint-sample \\n      --start=2025-02-10T00:00Z \\
      --end=2025-02-11T00:00Z \\
      --weighting-config=gs://redwood-configs/asstp/weights.yaml \\
      --output=gs://redwood-benches/asstp/2025-02-11/candidates.jsonl

Shard run config (YAML text example):
    name: asstp_shard_v1
    batch_size: 32
    seeds_per_sample: 3
    deterministic: false
    targeted_strata: [short_context, high_error_density]

Debugging and triage playbook (short)
------------------------------------
1. Identify sample cluster via stability index/regression alert.
2. Pull shard artifact and provenance_ids.
3. Re-run sample locally with identical runtime/kernels and quant flags.
4. If mismatch persists, run bisect automation:
   - isolate by model artifact (commit hash), quant profile, and routing bridge (region/instance-type)
   - reproduce with minimal prompt variant to confirm root cause
5. Publish triage summary and link to release ticket, include minimal repro and suggested mitigation.

Glossary
--------
- amplification: synthetic multiplication of samples in a stratum to increase detection power.
- shard: a packaged set of samples, config, and metadata used by the eval runner.
- provenance: production identifiers and metadata linking a sample back to live requests.
